title: console AI: a blueprint awaiting approval shows no sign on the chatbot launcher, so a user who closed the chat does not know an approval is waiting (objectui#2458 item 6)
body:
Path: ⑤ connect an Agent and have it complete a real business operation — the AI build surface | 缺项 (no item asserts a pending blueprint is visible from the launcher) | P5

Filed by the triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U`. It is a single-scope child of objectui#2458 (item 6), split on the maintainer's order (director `6006198254`). ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

Triage: lands in `packages/app-shell/src/layout/ConsoleChatbotFab.tsx` (rendered at `console/home/HomeLayout.tsx` about `:64`) and the `ChatDockLauncher` in `ChatDock.tsx` (about `:642`–`:660`) ⇒ `domain:ui`; rationale: both launchers are plain buttons with no pending-state signal.

## What is asked (objectui#2458 item 6)

While a proposed blueprint is **Awaiting Approval**, the launcher the user returns to (the console chatbot FAB, or the chat dock launcher) shows a passive marker, such as a dot or a count, that an approval is waiting. Opening the chat clears nothing by itself. The marker goes away when the blueprint is approved, rejected or superseded.

## Read on objectui `main` (`fc3c2cc1cf`)

- `ConsoleChatbotFab.tsx` (about `:42`–`:73`) and `ChatDockLauncher` (`ChatDock.tsx` about `:642`–`:660`) render no badge. Nothing under `layout/` reads a pending-blueprint state.
- The state exists: `hooks/useChatConversation.ts` (about `:162`–`:186`) caches the conversation's `proposedPlan`.
- The FAB is deliberately dependency-free (its header, about `:9`–`:13`). The signal must reach it without pulling the chat code into the first-load bundle. `scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` and `performance-budget.yml` will catch it if it does.

## Done when

- With a blueprint awaiting approval, both launchers show the marker, with an accessible name in all locales (no hard-coded English). With none awaiting, they show nothing.
- The marker follows the plan's state: it disappears on approve, reject or a newer proposal.
- The eager-closure budget stays green, so the FAB still imports no chat code.
- A test pins both launchers in both states, and is ablated once.
